notes: R skip: A motor-milestone checklist on video is a health screen of a small child's body, not capability evidence; it excludes a child with a physical disability and is kept ten years.
D edit: A three-item motor checklist is an observation note; filming children outdoors is heavier than the evidence, and the bundle of three skills should be recorded item by item.
E edit: The PE educator sees this in a session and notes each movement; filming thirty children for a count of three is not the lightest.
P edit: A video of my small child's body in play, kept ten years, for a movement any educator can see in a moment; a dated note is enough.

behaviours.statement: Returns to play after a small hurt or a lost game, once looked after.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the child back in play in the same session.
behaviours.counter_example: Returns to play only when an adult walks them back to the game.

notes: R edit: Sitting out after a hurt is a child's own choice, not a failing to list against them; the look-alike is a return steered by an adult, not the child's own.

before.counter_example: Sits out for the rest of the session after a small hurt.

behaviours.statement: Takes a full turn in an outdoor running or climbing game, moving in the way their own body moves.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the child take the turn from start to finish, with any aid they use.
behaviours.counter_example: Runs onto the field with the others and stands watching them take the turn.

notes: chair add: rights: physical competence shown as taking part with the body one has, open to a child with a disability, needing no milestone and no video; replaces the retired motor-milestone line. Revised on the seats' second look: rights: the counter no longer pictures the child who sits out.

behaviours.statement: Tells a classmate 'stop' or 'I am still using it', in words or signs, when the classmate reaches for or takes what they are using.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears or sees the words or sign given to the classmate before any adult steps in; the note holds the child's words, never the incident or the classmate.
behaviours.counter_example: Says 'stop' only after the educator has told the classmate to stop.

notes: chair add: development: nothing in the cell was the three-to-six-year-old holding their own ground in words; unafraid at this age is exactly that. Revised on the seats' second look: rights: the trigger is a classmate reaching for what the child is using, not being handled roughly; words or signs; the note never holds the incident.

behaviours.statement: Uses a strategy learned in class, such as breathing or stepping away, before responding in a conflict.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the strategy used in the moment, before the response, and notes the strategy alone, not the conflict or who else was in it.
behaviours.counter_example: Names the strategy afterwards but did not use it.

notes: R edit: Each record here also records a conflict; the note must hold the strategy alone, never the incident or the other child, or the file becomes a conflict log.

before.adult_sees: The educator sees the strategy used in the moment, before the response.

behaviours.statement: Keeps an agreement made with a classmate, such as a swap or a promise, without an adult enforcing it.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the agreement honoured with no adult involved.
behaviours.counter_example: Keeps the agreement only when reminded.

behaviours.statement: Invites a child standing alone at the edge of a game or group to join, before any adult suggests it.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the child alone at the edge and the invitation come from the classmate first.
behaviours.counter_example: Invites the child when an adult asks the group to.

notes: D edit: 'Left out' asks the observer to judge another child's state; a child alone at the edge of the game is what both educators can see.

before.statement: Invites a child who is left out into a game or a group, unprompted.
before.adult_sees: The educator sees the invitation come from the child.

behaviours.statement: Does their class responsibility, such as watering the plants, on a day when nobody reminded them, using their own way of remembering.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the job done before anyone has mentioned it that day, whatever memory aid the child uses.
behaviours.counter_example: Does the job after the educator glances at the job chart.

notes: R edit: 'Without reminders' bars a child who needs and uses a memory aid, a disability-linked need, from ever earning this; using one's own way of remembering is the independence.
D edit: 'For a week without reminders' is a pattern, which the record builds; one unprompted day is the occasion.
E edit: A week is not one occasion and I cannot hold seven days in my head; record the day it was done unprompted, and the records show the week.
chair edit: merged: the educator's one occasion (a day nobody reminded them) with the rights seat's memory aid.

before.statement: Carries out a class responsibility, such as plants or the library corner, for a week without reminders.
before.adult_sees: The educator sees the job done each day unprompted.
before.counter_example: Does the job on the first day only.

behaviours.statement: Shows a physical skill, such as skipping or catching, that an earlier record shows they could not yet do.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the skill done unaided and finds the earlier note saying the child could not yet do it.
behaviours.counter_example: Shows a skill they arrived at school already able to do.

notes: R edit: Video of a child's body across sessions is heavy identifiable data kept ten years and needs consent (DPDP Act); the educator seeing the skill shown holds this.
D edit: 'Over several sessions' is a pattern; the day the skill first works is the occasion, with earlier notes as the trail. Video is heavier than needed.
E edit: 'Over several sessions' is not one occasion; the occasion is the day the skill is shown, set against the earlier record.
P edit: As with the Foundational movement line: a dated note that the skill was shown after practice holds this; no video of my child's body is needed.
chair edit: all four seats moved video to a note; the educator's one occasion (the skill shown, an earlier note saying not yet) with development's counter.

before.statement: Learns a new physical skill, such as skipping or catching, by practising over several sessions and shows it.
before.adult_sees: The educator sees the skill shown after the practice sessions.
before.counter_example: Avoids the skill after the first failed try.

behaviours.statement: Accepts losing a game or a contest and congratulates the winner.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears the congratulation given to the winner.
behaviours.counter_example: Shakes the winner's hand only when an adult tells the players to.

notes: P edit: 'Blames the rules or the referee' is a portrait of a bad loser, not a look-alike; the near-miss is a congratulation given on instruction.

before.counter_example: Blames the rules or the referee.

behaviours.statement: Goes back to a classmate after a conflict to apologise or to sort it out, without being sent.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the approach made unprompted and notes the repair alone, not the conflict or the classmate.
behaviours.counter_example: Apologises when the educator stands beside them and waits for it.

notes: R edit: Every record here also records a conflict; note the repair alone; and a counter that has educators track who avoids whom for a week is surveillance of friendships.
D edit: The prompted apology is the over-count; avoiding the classmate is a non-example.
chair edit: rights and development converge on the prompted apology as the over-count; the week-long avoidance counter was surveillance of friendships.

before.adult_sees: The educator sees the approach made unprompted.
before.counter_example: Avoids the classmate for the rest of the week.

behaviours.statement: Delivers their agreed part to a team, such as attending a practice or handing in a section, on the date the team set.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the team's plan with the date and the part delivered on it.
behaviours.counter_example: Attends the sessions but leaves their part for others to deliver.

notes: R edit: 'Drops out when it stops being fun' reads a motive into leaving; a child may leave for illness, caring duties, transport or money the school never sees.
D edit: 'Across a term' is a pattern; the record builds it from dated deliveries, each of which is one observable occasion.
E edit: A term is not one occasion; I record each day the commitment was kept, and the term shows in the run of records.
P edit: 'when it stops being fun' judges a twelve-year-old's reasons; attendance without the promised part is the honest near-miss.
chair edit: parent and rights converge: attends but leaves the promised part undelivered.

before.counter_example: Drops out when it stops being fun.
before.statement: Keeps a commitment to a team, such as attending practice or delivering their part, across a term.
before.adult_sees: The educator sees the attendance or the part delivered through the term.

behaviours.statement: Speaks up when a classmate is being excluded or mocked, in the moment.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears the intervention as it happens and notes the speaking up alone; the mocking itself goes to the school's own process, not this record.
behaviours.counter_example: Joins the classmate's side once an adult has already stepped in.

notes: R edit: The note must hold the speaking up, never the bullying incident or the children in it, which belong to the anti-bullying process; the counter should not picture children laughing along.
P edit: 'Laughs along' files my child as complicit; the near-miss an educator actually confuses is speaking up after the moment instead of in it.
chair edit: rights seat's counter: telling the educator afterwards must not be the lesser act; the look-alike is joining once an adult has stepped in.

before.adult_sees: The educator hears the intervention as it happens.
before.counter_example: Laughs along and says later they did not agree.

behaviours.statement: Hands in a piece of work on its due date with the deadline written in their own planner the week before.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the planner entry dated at least a week earlier and the work in on the day.
behaviours.counter_example: Hands work in on time with a planner filled in that morning.

notes: D edit: 'A week with no missed submissions' is a pattern; the planner entry plus the on-time submission is the occasion.

before.statement: Manages their own deadlines and materials for a week using a planner, with no missed submissions.
before.adult_sees: The educator sees the planner used and nothing missed.
before.counter_example: Submits late and cites the planner.

behaviours.statement: Shows a training record for a goal about what they can do, such as a distance, with attempts dated across four or more weeks.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator reads the goal and attempt entries spanning four or more weeks, a record of what was done, never a body measure.
behaviours.counter_example: Records one attempt on the last day.

notes: R edit: A 'physical goal' can become a body-shape or scale goal for a twelve-year-old, a known harm; the record must hold what the child can do, never a body measure.
D edit: 'Over weeks' is a pattern; the occasion is the showing of the dated record, which carries the pattern.
chair edit: merged: development's dated record across four weeks as the occasion; rights' goal about what the child can do, never a body measure.

before.statement: Sets a physical goal, such as a distance or a routine, trains for it over weeks and records the attempts.
before.adult_sees: The educator reads the record of attempts across the weeks.

behaviours.statement: Asks a trusted adult for help with a personal difficulty before it affects their work.
behaviours.adult_sees: The adult approached records that the ask came before any missed work.
behaviours.counter_example: Mentions the difficulty only after a missed deadline.

notes: R skip: A child's disclosure of a personal difficulty to a trusted adult is confidential and may be about home; it must go to safeguarding, never to a file parents read.
D skip: 'Before it affects their work' is a counterfactual no observer can see, and the evidence is a private disclosure; help-seeking is real but this is not a recordable occasion.
E skip: Happens in private, not where I can see it; and the counter-example makes me grade a child on when they confided. Not a routine record.
P skip: A dated record that my child had 'a personal difficulty', kept ten years, is a confidence, not evidence; the help-seeking belongs with that adult, not in the file.

behaviours.statement: Tells the educator before a deadline that a piece of work will be late and proposes a new date.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears it before the date, with a new date offered.
behaviours.counter_example: Explains why the work is late after the deadline has passed.

notes: chair add: educator: the observable core of the retired trusted-adult line, asking before it affects work, with nothing private disclosed.

behaviours.statement: Takes on part of a classmate's share of a team task after the classmate says they cannot finish it, and tells the team.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears the classmate say so, sees the extra part done and hears the team told; the note names the part taken on, not the classmate or why.
behaviours.counter_example: Does the whole task alone without telling the team.

notes: chair add: parent: with the private-difficulty line retired, the cell needed a kind act that costs something and is safe to keep for ten years. Revised on the seats' second look: development: the classmate saying so is the visible trigger; rights: the note names the part taken on, never the classmate or why.

behaviours.statement: Mediates between two classmates in conflict so that both agree a way forward.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees both classmates accept the way forward and notes the mediation alone, not the dispute or who was in it.
behaviours.counter_example: Takes one side.

notes: R edit: The note must not carry two other children's dispute into the mediator's ten-year file; the mediation is the evidence, the dispute and its parties are not.

before.adult_sees: The educator sees both classmates accept the way forward.

behaviours.statement: Leads a team through a setback, such as a failed event, by re-planning with the team.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the re-plan made with the team present.
behaviours.counter_example: Assigns blame and re-plans alone.

behaviours.statement: Raises an unfairness affecting others through a school channel, such as council, and follows it through.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the matter raised in the channel and followed up, and notes the raising, not the complaint's content; a concern about an adult goes to the safeguarding lead instead.
behaviours.counter_example: Complains privately and lets it drop.

notes: R edit: A child's complaint about the school must never sit as content in their own file for future staff; note the act only; a concern about an adult is safeguarding.

before.adult_sees: The educator sees the matter raised in the channel and followed up.

behaviours.statement: Shows a term plan that holds both exam preparation and a project, with a dated change made after something slipped.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator reads the plan, the dated change and what prompted it.
behaviours.counter_example: Shows a plan written after the term ended.

notes: D edit: 'So both are delivered' is a term's outcome, not an occasion; the plan with a dated adjustment is what one moment shows.

before.statement: Plans a term with exams and projects so both are delivered, and adjusts the plan when something slips.
before.adult_sees: The educator sees the plan, the adjustment and both delivered.
before.counter_example: Drops the project to pass the exam.

behaviours.statement: Brings their own dated record of a physical practice kept across the year and names one change in it.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the child's own dated record and hears one change named from it.
behaviours.counter_example: Speaks about the practice in general terms with no record to show.

notes: D edit: 'Joins for the season and stops' is not a look-alike of reflecting; reflection without a record is the over-count.
E edit: A year is not one occasion; the occasion is the review where the child shows their own record, and the record is the lightest capture.

before.counter_example: Joins for the season and stops.
before.statement: Reflects at year end on a physical practice kept through the year, with the record of it.
before.adult_sees: The educator hears the reflection and sees the record.

behaviours.statement: Supports a peer through a difficulty over time and knows when to bring in an adult.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator learns of the support from the peer or sees the adult brought in at the right time.
behaviours.counter_example: Keeps a peer's serious difficulty secret from every adult.

notes: R skip: Evidence here is another child's private difficulty, learned by asking that child; peer support in serious matters is a safeguarding domain, not a capability record.
D edit: 'Knows when' is a mind read and 'over time' a pattern; adult_sees rests on hearsay. The observable moment is the bringing-in, with the peer's knowledge.
E skip: I would learn of this second-hand or only when it goes wrong; 'knows when' cannot be seen. Not something to record routinely.
P skip: 'Knows when' is a mind-read, and the record names another child's serious difficulty; a safeguarding moment is handled by people, never filed as routine evidence.

behaviours.statement: Brings a classmate who missed a session up to date on what was agreed and what they missed, without being asked.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the catch-up happen before the next session, unprompted.
behaviours.counter_example: Forwards the notes when the classmate asks for them.

notes: chair add: parent and rights, in near-identical words: a kind act toward a peer that names no one's trouble, in place of the retired peer-difficulty line.

behaviours.statement: Stops an argument that has reached raised voices by proposing a break and a time to return to it.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears the break proposed with a time to return and sees the argument pause; the note holds the proposal, not the argument or who was in it.
behaviours.counter_example: Walks away from the argument without a word about returning.

notes: chair add: development: emotional regulation, named in the capability, had no Secondary behaviour; this is its 14-to-16 form in observable terms. Revised on the seats' second look: rights: the note holds the proposal, not the argument or who was in it.

could_not.detail: Emotional regulation is written only as actions a person could see; the regulation itself is not observable. The physical behaviours are placeholders for a movement checklist the school should adopt, such as TGMD-style criteria, which this prompt cannot author.

capabilities.name: Society, ethics & planet
capabilities.observable_at_16: Can examine trade-offs, understand systems and consider consequences beyond the self.

behaviours.statement: Waters a plant or feeds the class animal on their day, and checks it is alright.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the care given and the check made.
behaviours.counter_example: Waters it when an adult hands over the can.

behaviours.statement: Puts waste into the right bin, wet, dry or paper, without prompting.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator watches the bins after snack and sees the right one chosen with nobody pointing.
behaviours.counter_example: Puts waste in the nearest bin.

notes: E edit: Bins are used after snack and at clean-up, not in circle; the setting should be one educators recognise and adult_sees should say when to look.

before.adult_sees: The educator sees the right bin chosen unprompted.

behaviours.statement: Shares a material, such as crayons or blocks, with a classmate who has none, without being asked.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the share come from the child.
behaviours.counter_example: Shares after an adult says 'share'.

notes: R edit: Snack-sharing crosses allergy and family dietary rules, and 'a classmate who has none' turns another child's missing food, a home matter, into a note; materials carry neither risk.

before.statement: Shares a material or a snack with a classmate who has none, without being asked.

behaviours.statement: Notices that a classmate or a younger child needs something and gets it for them.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the need met without an adult pointing it out.
behaviours.counter_example: Notices and tells an adult only when asked.

notes: D edit: As drafted it records the same evidence as shares-without-being-asked; help to a younger child is distinct and shows 'beyond the self' at four to seven.
E skip: Same moment as shares-without-being-asked in this cell and comforts-a-classmate under self-and-relationships; one act would be filed three times.
chair skip: educator's skip stands: the same moment as shares-without-being-asked in this cell and comforts-a-classmate under self-and-relationships; one act would be filed three times.

behaviours.statement: Says what would be fair for everyone when a share or a turn is in dispute, including a child who is not their friend.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears a fairness that applies to everyone, including a child the speaker was not playing with.
behaviours.counter_example: Says fair means getting their own way.

notes: R edit: An audio recording of a playground dispute puts other children's voices into one child's file without their consent; the educator hearing the fairness proposed holds this.
E edit: Nobody records audio in the playground; a note of the fairness the child proposed holds it.
chair edit: close to uses-words-to-settle-a-dispute under communication; re-worded to the ethical act, fairness for everyone including a child not their friend.

before.statement: Says what would be fair when a game or a share is in dispute, such as taking turns.
before.adult_sees: The educator hears a fairness that applies to everyone.

behaviours.statement: Leaves a shared space, such as the reading corner, tidy for the next group.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the space left ready.
behaviours.counter_example: Tidies only their own spot.

notes: E skip: Same moment as puts-materials-back-ready-for-next under learning-and-agency; a colleague and I would file one tidy-up twice.
chair skip: educator's skip stands: the same tidy-up as puts-materials-back-ready-for-next under learning-and-agency.

behaviours.statement: Turns off a tap left running or a light left on in an empty room, with nobody asking.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the tap or switch closed by the child before anyone speaks.
behaviours.counter_example: Turns it off when the educator points at it.

notes: chair add: educator: after the two duplicate lines were retired the cell held only sharing and care; water and light are things a Nursery child can act on.

behaviours.statement: Picks up litter that is not their own from the playground and puts it in the bin.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees litter picked up that the child did not drop.
behaviours.counter_example: Puts their own wrapper in the bin.

notes: chair add: educator: distinct from sorting waste into the right bin; acting for a shared space one did not dirty.

behaviours.statement: Votes in a class choice and goes along with the result when their choice loses.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the vote cast and the child join the chosen activity after their choice lost.
behaviours.counter_example: Joins the winning activity having voted for it.

notes: chair add: development: accepting a group decision that went against you is the four-to-seven-year-old's first civic act; the cell had care and sharing but no group decision.

behaviours.statement: Handles a living thing found outdoors, such as a snail or a worm, gently and puts it back where it was.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the creature handled without harm and returned to its place.
behaviours.counter_example: Keeps the creature in a box to show the class later.

notes: chair add: development: the planet appeared only as the class plant and the bins; care for a wild living thing is distinct and reachable at three.

behaviours.statement: Reports a figure they measured about the school's use of water, paper or power, and says how they measured it.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears the figure, what it is about, and how it was measured.
behaviours.counter_example: Reports a figure found online about schools in general.

notes: chair edit: the same measurement as uses-a-measuring-tool under knowledge; re-worded to the civic act, reporting a figure about the school's own use.

before.statement: Measures or counts something about the campus, such as water used or plants grown, and reports it.
before.adult_sees: The educator sees the measurement taken and the report.
before.counter_example: Guesses the number.

behaviours.statement: Proposes and carries out one way to reduce waste in a class activity and checks whether it worked.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the change made and the check afterwards.
behaviours.counter_example: Proposes a way and does not try it.

behaviours.statement: Explains a school or class rule by the reason for it, not just 'because it is the rule'.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears the reason, not the rule repeated.
behaviours.counter_example: Says the rule is the rule.

behaviours.statement: Names who else is affected by a decision in a story or a class choice, beyond themselves.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears others named and how they are affected.
behaviours.counter_example: Names only how it affects them.

behaviours.statement: Does a task that helps someone outside the class, such as reading to younger children, and reports it.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the task done and the report.
behaviours.counter_example: Helps a classmate inside the class and reports it as service.

notes: P edit: 'Is assigned the task and leaves early' reads as skiving; the near-miss is help given inside the class and counted as service outside it.

before.counter_example: Is assigned the task and leaves early.

behaviours.statement: Keeps a promise made to the group, such as bringing materials, and says so if it cannot be kept.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the promise kept, or hears it explained in time.
behaviours.counter_example: Forgets the promise and says nothing.

notes: R edit: 'Bringing materials' makes the promise depend on what a home can supply, so a child who cannot is read against the family; a part of the task does not.
chair skip: one promise kept, two rows: keeps-an-agreement-made-with-a-classmate under self-and-relationships records the same act.

behaviours.statement: Collects data on a local issue, such as traffic or water at school, and presents the findings to those who can act on them.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the findings presented to a person or body who can act on the issue, not only to the class.
behaviours.counter_example: Presents the findings to the class only, with no one who could act on them in the room.

notes: P edit: 'from the internet as their own' is a plagiarism charge; the near-miss is published data standing in for the child's own.
chair edit: the same investigation as investigates-an-open-question under creation; re-worded to the civic act, presenting findings to those who can act.

before.counter_example: Presents findings from the internet as their own.
before.statement: Investigates a local issue, such as traffic or water at school, with data they collected, and presents findings.
before.adult_sees: The educator sees the findings rest on data the child collected.

behaviours.statement: Sets out both sides of a real decision, such as cost against waste, before recommending one, and names who bears the cost.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator reads both sides set out and the person or group who bears the cost named.
behaviours.counter_example: Recommends the option with no downside named.

notes: chair edit: the same trade-off as pitches-a-solution-with-trade-offs under creation; re-worded to the ethical act, both sides and who bears the cost.

before.statement: Weighs a trade-off in a real decision, such as cost against waste, and recommends with reasons.
before.adult_sees: The educator reads both sides of the trade-off and the recommendation.

behaviours.statement: States the strongest case for each side of a civic question before giving their own view.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator hears each side made well before the child's view, and notes the two cases made, not the view the child gave.
behaviours.counter_example: Gives their own view and a token version of the other side.

notes: R edit: A video of a twelve-year-old's own view on a civic question, kept ten years, is a record of a child's politics; note the two cases made, not the view.
D edit: Two cases made before the child's own view is heard once and noted; video is heavier than needed.
E edit: This is a lesson discussion, not a staged debate; a note that both sides were made before the child's own view holds it.

before.adult_sees: The educator hears each side made well before the child's view.

behaviours.statement: Changes a plan after seeing that it would harm someone else, and says why.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the change and hears the reason.
behaviours.counter_example: Keeps the plan and apologises later.

behaviours.statement: Organises a service activity with classmates, from plan to delivery, for people outside school.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the plan and the delivery, with the people served described and not photographed or named.
behaviours.counter_example: Joins a service activity organised by adults.

notes: R edit: The artefact must not carry photographs or names of the people served, who are third parties and often in a vulnerable position; describe the service, not the persons.

before.adult_sees: The educator sees the plan, the delivery and the people served.

behaviours.statement: Owns a mistake that affected others, tells those affected and puts it right.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees those affected told and the repair made, and notes the owning and the repair, not the mistake's detail or who was affected.
behaviours.counter_example: Puts it right quietly without telling those affected.

notes: R edit: A record of owning a mistake also files the mistake for ten years; the note holds the owning and the repair, not what went wrong or who was affected.

before.adult_sees: The educator sees those affected told and the repair made.

behaviours.statement: Models a system, such as the school's water or a market, with its feedback loops, and uses it to explain an outcome.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees feedback loops in the model and an outcome explained by them.
behaviours.counter_example: Draws a diagram with arrows and no feedback.

behaviours.statement: Applies an ethical framework to a real dilemma, names the trade-offs, decides and defends it.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator reads the framework applied, the trade-offs and the defence.
behaviours.counter_example: Decides on instinct and adds a framework label.

behaviours.statement: Engages a public body, business or community group on an issue through the school, with a documented exchange.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the exchange documented, sent through the school and carrying no home address or personal details of the child.
behaviours.counter_example: Writes a letter that is never sent.

notes: R edit: A minor's approach to an outside body goes through the school and carries no home details; the filed exchange must not become a record of the child's politics.

before.statement: Engages a public body, business or community group on an issue, with a documented exchange.
before.adult_sees: The educator sees the exchange documented.

behaviours.statement: Changes something they do at school, such as printing or single-use packaging, after seeing evidence of its harm, and names the evidence.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the changed practice at school and hears the evidence named.
behaviours.counter_example: Pledges the change publicly and shows a log begun the day before.

notes: R edit: A 'personal habit' at home puts the family's diet, consumption or the child's health on file and needs home surveillance to verify; a school habit is seen by the educator.
D edit: A home habit kept for a term is self-report of private conduct, not observation; a dated log the child shows is the occasion, and it need not be at home.
E skip: Nothing here happens where an educator can see it, and a term is not one occasion; it rests on the child's own claim about home.
P edit: What my child does at home is not the school's to record, and the evidence would be my child's word on our household; keep it to school.

chair edit: the educator skipped a home habit over a term; the parent and rights seats offered a school-visible version, which meets every objection: the occasion is the day the change is made and the evidence named.

before.statement: Changes a personal habit on evidence of its harm to others or the environment, and keeps the change for a term.
before.adult_sees: The educator hears the evidence named and sees the change kept.
before.counter_example: Pledges the change publicly and stops within a week.

behaviours.statement: Presents the term's record of a service commitment they led, showing what changed for the people served.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator reads dated entries across the term and a stated change for those served, written without their names or private circumstances.
behaviours.counter_example: Runs a one-day event and reports it as sustained.

notes: R edit: The people served are third parties, often in a vulnerable position; their names and circumstances must not enter a child's school file, so the record describes change, not persons.
D edit: 'Over a term' is a pattern; the presentation of the dated record is the occasion an educator can record.
chair edit: merged: development's presented record as the occasion; rights' record written without the names or private circumstances of those served.

before.adult_sees: The educator reads the record of what changed for those served.
before.statement: Leads a service commitment over a term, with a record of what changed for the people served.

behaviours.statement: Holds a public role in the school, such as council or event lead, and accounts for decisions to those affected.
behaviours.adult_sees: The educator sees the accounting made to those affected.
behaviours.counter_example: Holds the role and reports to adults only.

could_not.detail: At the Foundational stage 'consequences beyond the self' can only show as sharing, tidying and care, which overlap with kind behaviours under self-and-relationships; the founders may merge or move them.
